title.es: Preparación para un panel de discusión

objective.en: Use discussion moves such as building on an idea, asking a question and disagreeing politely, then prepare and give a turn.
objective.es: Usar recursos de discusión como desarrollar una idea, hacer una pregunta y no estar de acuerdo con cortesía, y luego preparar y dar un turno.

success.en: I can name the moves speakers use in a discussion.
success.es: Puedo nombrar los recursos que usan los oradores en una discusión.

success.en: I can build on another speaker's idea.
success.es: Puedo desarrollar la idea de otro orador.

success.en: I can ask a question that moves the discussion forward.
success.es: Puedo hacer una pregunta que haga avanzar la discusión.

success.en: I can give a clear turn with a reason and an example.
success.es: Puedo dar un turno claro con una razón y un ejemplo.

narrative: Your school is discussing whether the school day should start an hour later. Sol the Conversation Guide has recorded a short panel discussion. Study how the speakers talk, practice with Sol, and prepare your own turn. The panel and its speakers are made up for practice.

scene.alt: A small stage with red curtains and a spotlight. Four chairs sit in a half circle with a speech bubble and a book on a stool in front.

vocab.def: To add to what someone else said.
To make an idea clearer by asking or explaining.
A point that disagrees with another point.
Your chance to speak in a discussion.

items.prompt: Read part of the panel discussion. Notice what each speaker does.

sources.title: Speaker A (Maya)
text: I think school should start an hour later because teenagers need more sleep. Studies say that tired students learn less.

sources.title: Speaker B (Omar)
text: Building on what Maya said, a later start could also help students arrive on time. However, it might make after-school activities end very late.

sources.title: Speaker C (Lena)
text: Could you clarify what you mean by very late, Omar? I wonder if clubs could start earlier in the day.

sources.title: Speaker D (Raj)
text: I respectfully disagree. A later start would make families' morning plans harder, so I would try a half-hour change first.

items.prompt: Which discussion move is each sentence?

cards.text: Building on what Maya said, a later start could also help students arrive on time.
cards.why: The speaker starts from what someone else said and adds to it.

cards.text: Could you clarify what you mean by very late?
cards.why: The speaker asks to make an idea clearer.

cards.text: I respectfully disagree. A later start would make mornings harder for families.
cards.why: The speaker says a different view in a polite way.

cards.text: To add to that, sleep also helps students remember.
cards.why: The speaker adds a new detail to someone else's point.
The speaker asks for more information.

items.prompt: Practice with Sol. Pick questions, and write one question of your own.

say: Name the speaker and repeat the idea in a few words. Then add a reason, an example or a new detail.
Try: 'Could you explain what you mean by ...?' It shows you are listening.
Say what you agree with first. Then say 'however' or 'I see it differently' and give your reason.
Ready to practice the moves? What would you like to ask?

options.label: How do I build on another speaker's idea?
How do I ask a clarifying question politely?
How do I disagree without being rude?

compose.label: Write your own question for Sol

checks.label: Ends with a question mark and asks something

say: I am not sure. You could ask about building on ideas, clarifying or disagreeing.
Good. Now prepare your own turn.

items.prompt: Write what you will say in the panel about starting school an hour later. State your position, build on one speaker by name, and give a reason.
items.purpose: Sol will use your notes to run your turn.

checks.label: Builds on a speaker by name
Includes a question for the panel

ladder.model: Model: I support a later start because sleep helps students focus. Building on what Maya said, tired students also make more mistakes. Could the school try a half-hour change first?
ladder.frame: I think ___ because ___. Building on what ___ said, ___. Could we ___?
ladder.cue: Position. Build on a speaker. Reason.

items.prompt: Strengthen your turn. Add an example, and answer a different view politely with however or I respectfully disagree.
items.purpose: A strong turn has a reason, an example and a response.

ladder.model: Model: For example, some students sleep only six hours. However, I understand that families need time in the morning, so a half-hour change could help both groups.
ladder.frame: For example, ___. However, I understand ___, so ___.

items.prompt: Give your turn in the panel in about one minute. Name a speaker you build on, give a reason and an example.

ladder.frame: I think ___ because ___. Building on what ___ said, ___. For example, ___.

selfChecks.label: I built on a speaker by name.
I spoke clearly and not too fast.

items.prompt: Which sentence builds on another speaker's idea?

options.label: That is wrong.
options.fb: This does not add to the idea.

options.label: Building on Sam's point, students could also vote on the plan.
I do not care.
options.fb: This does not add to the idea.

options.label: Next topic, please.
options.fb: This moves away from the idea.

items.why: Building on means starting from another speaker's point and adding to it, as this sentence does with Sam's point about the plan.

endings.title: A strong panel turn
endings.text: The room listens as you speak. 'You built on a speaker, gave a reason and an example, and answered another view respectfully,' says Sol. 'That is a strong turn.'

endings.title: Your turn is ready
endings.text: Sol nods. 'You stated a position and a reason,' says Sol. 'Next time, add an example and answer another view politely.'

skill.en: joining a discussion: building on ideas, asking questions and disagreeing politely
skill.es: participar en una discusión: desarrollar ideas, hacer preguntas y no estar de acuerdo con cortesía

talk.en: Ask: 'Whose idea did you build on? What question did you ask? How did you disagree politely?'
talk.es: Pregunta: '¿La idea de quién desarrollaste? ¿Qué pregunta hiciste? ¿Cómo mostraste desacuerdo con cortesía?'
